items.excerpt: Daft Punk's Thomas Bangalter says he has no interest in the creative use of AI, arguing that prompting is the opposite of his process: "We need to surprise ourself and to be more and more unpredictable, and we can't have technology do that for us." A rare craft-level rejection of prompt-based composition from a producer whose whole catalogue was built on machines.
items.title: Daft Punk's Thomas Bangalter explains why he's "not interested in the creative use of AI"

items.excerpt: MusicTech re-tested nine AI stem separation tools — LANDR, MVSEP, Moises and others — head to head on the same source material to see which now splits a mix cleanly enough for real remix and sampling work. The verdict: the quality gap between cloud services and DAW-native splitters has narrowed sharply in 2026.
items.title: I tested 9 of the best stem separation tools. Here's how they compare

items.excerpt: HeadRush 5.1 adds native Neural Amp Modeler capture support and Tone3000 integration to its Prime modellers, letting players load "hundreds of thousands" of community-trained neural amp captures straight onto the rig. Neural tone-cloning stops being a nerd side-project and becomes a stock feature of mainstream guitar hardware.
items.title: HeadRush rolls out Tone3000 integration and native support for NAM captures on its amp and effects modellers

items.excerpt: Gearnews maps out which pedals, multi-FX units and plugins already support Neural Amp Modeler A2 just months after the open neural-capture format shipped. It is a snapshot of an open-source ML model quietly becoming the default tone-capture standard across an entire hardware category.
items.title: NAM A2 Pedals & Software: This Gear Supports Neural Amp Modeler A2 in 2026!

items.excerpt: Synthesizer V maker Dreamtonics has teased an unannounced release with a single cryptic line — "human nuance is not a switch." The vocal-synthesis studio behind the most-used AI singing engine in production is signalling a pitch about expressive control rather than raw generation.
items.title: Dreamtonics tease upcoming release

items.excerpt: IK Multimedia's Tonex 2.0 public beta brings deeper ToneNET integration, up to 220 new Premium V2 Tone Models and a rebuilt interface for finding and editing machine-modelled amp captures. The redesign is aimed squarely at the browse-and-audition problem that appears once a library of neural captures gets big enough.
items.title: IK Multimedia launch Tonex 2.0 beta

items.excerpt: Composer-engineer Austin Rockman has released Reflector, a free open-source macOS workstation that uses machine learning to make a messy sample library actually navigable — surfacing sounds by timbral similarity instead of filename. A rare case of ML applied to the boring part of production rather than to generation.
items.title: Reflector is a FREE open-source sample discovery workstation for macOS

items.excerpt: Suno's Voices feature — record or upload yourself singing, then generate new songs in your own voice — is now on iOS and Android, with a limited version opened to free users. Consented self-cloning moves from a paid desktop experiment to a default mobile capability.
items.keyword: AI vocal cloning / consented voice model
items.title: Suno brings its voice clone tool to iOS and Android, opens a limited version to free users

items.excerpt: Saregama, India's oldest label, is generating AI music videos for catalogue songs whose original visuals it never owned, repackaging decades of audio-only recordings for Gen Z feeds. A concrete production-design use case for generative video sitting on top of a legacy music catalogue.
items.title: Saregama is using AI to make music videos for songs whose visuals it never owned

items.excerpt: Distributor Symphonic is embedding ArtyShield's voice- and recording-protection tooling directly inside SymphonicMS, so independent artists can flag and defend against unauthorised AI use of their voice from the same dashboard they release from. Anti-cloning defence becomes a checkbox in the distribution workflow.
items.title: Symphonic partners with ArtyShield to give artists tools that protect their music and voices from unauthorized AI use

items.excerpt: AI companies increasingly promise they can "unlearn" a musician's work after training, but the new Machine Unlearning Research Hub argues that removing data from a trained model is largely infeasible today. Hypebot translates the research into what an artist should actually ask for when a platform offers opt-out.
items.title: Can AI Unlearn Music? What Musicians Need to Know

items.excerpt: AI agents are quietly taking over the back office of music companies — delivery QC, metadata cleanup, trend monitoring and even early A&R screening. DMN separates what is actually shipping from what is still a pitch deck, with a look at how release ops teams are restructuring around it.
items.title: How AI Agents Are Quietly Automating Music Companies: From A&R to Release Ops

items.excerpt: Google's Flow Music Spaces update pulls song creation, section-level editing, stem splitting and video generation into a single AI workspace. It is Google's clearest attempt yet to make one surface cover the whole track-to-visual pipeline rather than shipping isolated music models.
items.title: Can Google Build the All-in-One AI Music Studio? Flow Music Gets Song Creation, Editing, and Stem Splitting

items.excerpt: With Spotify declining to label AI-generated tracks, third-party databases have started classifying them for listeners themselves. An unofficial metadata layer is forming around the streaming catalogue — and it will shape what "human-made" means on a release page.
items.title: Spotify Won't Label AI Music—So Third-Parties Are Cropping Up to Categorize It Instead

items.excerpt: Music Ally revisits the Fenix Flexin "Rubberz" case, where a viral track drew AI-generation accusations — and where the artist's own defence was that nearly every DAW now has AI in it somewhere. The piece is a sharp look at how blurry "AI-generated" has become as a production label.
items.title: Is that viral Fenix Flexin song AI-generated after all? (And if so, what does that mean?)

items.excerpt: Sylvan Esso walk through making Ow ∞ in their self-built Betty's studio, framing the record's deliberate human mess as the thing generative models can't reach — "Suno isn't coming up with that anytime soon" — and explain why they pulled their catalogue from Spotify.
items.title: Sylvan Esso on the making of Ow ∞, their self-built studio and why they pulled their music from Spotify

items.excerpt: Fender CEO Edward "Bud" Cole walks back his comparison of cover songs to "analogue AI" after a musician backlash, while still arguing AI can be a genuine learning tool for players. A live test of how instrument brands are allowed to talk about AI to their own users.
items.title: Fender CEO clarifies his controversial comments comparing cover songs to AI
